ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image shows a cyclic carbohydrate in a chair-like ring form. There is a ring oxygen atom on the right side of the ring, and the carbon skeleton bears several hydroxyl groups. The ring contains five carbon positions plus one oxygen, and there is an exocyclic carbon substituent bearing an OH group, giving six carbons in the sugar framework. Reasoning: The anomeric carbon is the carbon attached to the ring oxygen on the right; it also bears an OH group and an H. An anomeric carbon bearing H indicates that the cyclic form came from an aldehyde group rather than a ketone group. Since the carbohydrate has six carbons and is aldehyde-derived, it is an aldohexose.

Next locate the anomeric carbon attached to the ring oxygen and bearing an OH and an H; this shows the cyclic form came from an aldehyde rather than a ketone. Since the molecule has six carbons and is aldehyde-derived, answer that the carbohydrate is an aldohexose.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct structural-classification route: infer both the carbon count and carbonyl origin from the cyclic sugar drawing, then combine the two classification terms.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the carbohydrate structure in the image as a cyclic monosaccharide: a ring containing one oxygen, multiple hydroxyl groups, one exocyclic CH2OH-type side chain, and an anomeric carbon bearing both H and OH. Count the carbon framework as six carbons total.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt only to know that the requested output is the type of carbohydrate shown; there is no additional textual data needed for classification.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use carbohydrate nomenclature: a six-carbon monosaccharide is a hexose; if its open-chain carbonyl would be an aldehyde, indicated in the cyclic hemiacetal by an anomeric carbon bearing H and OH rather than two carbon substituents, it is an aldose. Combining aldose + hexose gives aldohexose.
